r: Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, Orissa granted by **Shah Alam II**
First Parliamentary intervention – the Company to pay the British treasury **£400,000 a year**; dividend raised to/capped at **10%**
Select Committee (**Burgoyne**) and Secret Committee; the Company sought a £1 million loan → **Regulating Act, 1773**
**First step** by the British Parliament to **control and regulate** the Company; recognised its political and administrative functions; foundation of central administration
**Governor of Bengal → Governor-General of Bengal** (**Warren Hastings**), with a **council of four** (Francis, Clavering, Monson, Barwell)
Majority decisions; GG only a **casting vote** (no veto) → Hastings outvoted
**Directors to submit** to the British Government all communications on the **civil and military affairs of Bengal** and the **revenues of India**
Kept (not abolished); the Board of Control came only in 1784
**Supreme Court at Calcutta (Fort William), 1774** – India's **first Supreme Court**, set up by the **Regulating Act**
Its jurisdiction vis-à-vis the Council was **left vague**
**Madras (1801)** – serving the Madras Presidency incl. Andhra – and Bombay (1823)

**Six commissioners** (incl. Chancellor of the Exchequer and a Secretary of State) – **political** affairs
**Commercial** affairs → **double government** (ended by the GoI Act 1858)
Company territories first called **"British possessions in India"**
GG could **override his Council** in special cases and also be **Commander-in-Chief**
Extended the override to all future GGs and presidency Governors
